PagerDuty Bot: INCIDENT P1 — elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate across multiple regions, start: 2026-03-15T12:03:09Z :rotating_light:
Jordan: oncall here, looking. which regions?
Priya: seeing spikes from us-east-1 and eu-west-1, but traces show origin DNS failures before backend errors.
Tina: neteng - Cloudflare resolver metrics show a spike in SERVFAIL from a subset of their edge resolvers hitting our geo DNS -> looks like Route53 health checks flapping for the eu-west record.
Eli: support -> multiple customers reporting increased 502/504s, notably acct acme-inc (EU) and a couple of mobile clients in APAC.
Jordan: @Priya can you paste the dig output from us-east vs eu-west?
Priya: here, quick dig results: ```
; us-east-1 (172.31.0.5)
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.example
52.14.23.8

; eu-west-1 (10.0.0.12)
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.example
; received SERVFAIL

; direct to our nameserver (ns-1.route53.example)
$ dig @ns-1.route53.example api.redwood-inference.example +short
52.14.23.8
54.76.11.9
```
Jordan: so some resolvers are getting SERVFAIL, others are fine -> negative caching means clients keep failing. That matches Cloudflare's resolver spike.
Tina: looks like Route53 health checks for the eu-west routing policy are flapping — maybe transient ROUTE53 backend issue or our health check endpoint timing out from certain VPCs. I'm seeing increased latency to the health-check endpoints from a handful of AZs.
inc-bot: Runbook: GeoDNS outages -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/geodns (action: reduce TTL, enable failover to secondary NS, contact providers)
Jordan: mitigation plan: 1) reduce DNS TTL to 60s for api redirection 2) add a failover record to point traffic to global anycast A record 3) open ticket with Cloudflare + AWS Route53 4) notify customers in status page. Starting TTL change now.
Priya: doing TTL change on Route53 now (updating record-set TTL to 60). Propagation may take ~1-2 mins for new queries.
Eli: I'll draft status message for status.redwood.ai — short update: "Partial outage for API in EU and APAC due to upstream DNS resolver failures; mitigations in progress." Want to avoid overpromising.
Tina: also enabling secondary authoritative nameserver (ns-backup) as immediate failover via Route53 failover policy. Adding the backup NS now.
Jordan: while TTL propagates, let's push a temporary client-side fix for Dedicated customers: change resolver in our VPC DHCP option to prefer internal resolver 10.0.0.53 -> will reduce reliance on public resolvers. Priya can you coordinate?
Priya: done for dedicated VPCs, pushed config. Mobile/public customers still hit Cloudflare.
Cloudflare Support: thanks for the heads-up, we see elevated SERVFAIL from our LAX and AMS PoPs to your authoritative nameservers; opening internal escalation. Can you share trace/dig logs?
Jordan: pasted dig outputs above, and I'll provide a pcap if requested.
Eli: status page updated and incident tagged P1. Customers notified via email for impacted accounts.
Tina: Route53 responded (automated): "We are investigating health check flapping for your hosted zone; recommended to ensure health check endpoints are reachable from all AWS health check locations." Also flagged for on-call review.
Jordan: Next: monitor 5xx rate and DNS error rate. @Priya / @Tina keep me posted. I'm escalating to incident lead.
Priya: DNS errors trending down after TTL change and ns-backup activation, 5xx rate falling from 7% -> 1.2% in last 4 mins.
Jordan: good. We'll keep failover active for another hour, then slowly roll back once stable. handing off primary oncall to Priya at 12:15 UTC for continued monitoring.
Priya: taking over @ 12:15 UTC. I'm running periodic dig checks and cloud provider tickets are open.
Eli: customer acme-inc acknowledged receiving email and will monitor. No new support escalations in last 10 mins.
Cloudflare Support: update - a subset of our edge resolvers were returning SERVFAIL due to transient TCP connection failures to two of your authoritative IPs; we have rerouted resolvers and cleared caches. Suggest keeping TTL lowered while caches flush.
Tina: confirming internal metrics show resolvers cleared their negative cache entries. Good to see qps normalize.
Priya: reducing monitoring alert thresholds temporarily to avoid noise. Will prepare RCA draft after stabilizes.
Jordan: thanks team. I'm closing the active paging for now; Priya you'll own the RCA and postmortem. Please include timeline, root cause hypothesis (health-check timeout + resolver negative caching), and mitigation actions (lower TTL, add ns-backup, update health-check endpoints to be reachable from all AWS locations, update runbook).
Priya: noted, starting RCA doc. Will ping when draft is ready for review.
inc-bot: Incident resolved (service returned to normal). Incident duration ~32m.
Eli: marking incident on status page as resolved and linking the RCA draft once ready.
Jordan: thumbs up :thumbsup: great response.
Priya: handing off full post-incident to Tina for network followup on nameserver reachability. Tina?
Tina: will open follow-up tickets with AWS (Route53) and Cloudflare for deeper telemetry and to confirm they won't reintroduce the caching issue.
Cloudflare Support: will share PoP-specific logs in the escalation ticket.
Priya: last check - 5xx rate = 0.2% (baseline). Closing monitoring if stable for next 30m.
Jordan: last_message note: keeping the incident doc linked in #postmortems.
